LLM_description:
Situation:
Multiple supply depots in the corps rear (e.g., Supply Depot Bravo, Depot Echo, Depot Lima) are supporting forward units under contact (e.g., Infantry Battalion Falcon at Forward Operating Base Alpha and Armored Battalion Wolf along the eastern corridor). Main supply routes are contested with intermittent interdiction, IED threat, and limited engineer assets for route clearance. Alternate mountain passes are narrow and weather-affected; valley routes are exposed to direct fire and ambush. Airlift is constrained; operations rely on ground convoys. Movement Control Teams must coordinate departures by day, deconflict routes, and manage staging points.

Mission:
Deliver priority supplies (ammunition, fuel, medical and life support) from rear depots to the forward units across the operational window, minimizing total operational cost comprising transport costs, shortage penalties, vehicle deployment costs, and fixed route security risk costs, while maintaining combat readiness and freedom of movement.

Execution/Concept:
- Allocation and Flow: Determine daily shipments from each depot to each unit by supply type. Do not exceed depot capacity by supply and day. Meet unit demands each day; if shortfalls occur, they accrue penalty costs.
- Vehicle Utilization: Convert shipments to volume using supply-specific volume factors. Loaded volume on a given depot–unit route and day must not exceed the product of vehicle capacity and vehicles dispatched on that route–day. Vehicle deployments incur a per-vehicle cost.
- Route Activation and Risk: Vehicles can only move on routes explicitly activated for that depot–unit pairing on a given day. Activating any route (sending any vehicles) incurs a fixed Risk Cost that represents security overhead (escort teams, EOD and engineer route clearance, ISR tasking, and QRF standby). This fixed Risk Cost is charged once per activated route–day, regardless of the number of vehicles.
- Fleet Management: Total vehicles dispatched across all routes on a given day cannot exceed the available fleet. Prioritize consolidating shipments onto fewer activated routes to reduce repeated fixed risk charges, balanced against capacity constraints and exposure risk.
- Threat and Terrain: Route selection must account for known hazards, likely ambush locations, bridge limitations, and choke points. Engineer support will be focused on critical corridors; alternates will be used to mitigate disruption. Night movements may reduce detection but complicate clearance and recovery.
- Command and Control: Movement Control Teams and convoy commanders will synchronize departure timings, security packages, and route clearance windows. Depots will stage loads to meet time-on-route requirements. Units will provide receipt and confirm resupply to close the loop on demand fulfillment.
